text:
ashley: ran perf+nsys on prefetch/kv-cache branch — seeing CPU-side spikes during warmup. flamegraph attached (perf collapse below).

jin: can u paste perf command + sample? also which workload (batch size / seq len)?

ashley: ```
perf record -F 200 -g --call-graph dwarf -p 12345 -- sleep 45
nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=none -o nsys_prefetch ./bench_prefetch.sh
```

kai: workload = synthetic: 8 reqs, bs=16, seq=512, kv warmups enabled. saw kvcache evictions at ~3s into run.

matt: flame shows big hot in python: Scheduler.poll -> BatchBuilder.add -> PyObject_Call. looks like GIL bounce. any Cythonized hotspots?

ashley: stackcollapse snippet:
python3;Scheduler.poll 35.4%
python3;tokenizers._fast_tokenize 20.1%
libc;memcpy 5.0%
runtime;select 4.2%

jin: nsys kernel timeline shows frequent small launches of kernel `kv_prefetch_stage` with ~100-200us kernels alternating with heavy `matmul_q4` kernels — kernel mux may be choosing wrong kernel variant.

kai: i think kernel selector falls back to cpu-copy path when sequence % 64 != 0; that causes memcpy host->device and forces sync on stream. explains the tiny kernel + stalls.

matt: repro + quick mitigations:
```
# repro (on perf box)
CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 ./bench_prefetch.sh
# mitigations to try:
# - use pinned host buffers
# - align seq lengths to 64
# - increase batch size to >32 to amortize launch overhead
```

ashley: pinned buffers + bumping batch to 32 reduced syscall / kernel-launch rate by ~6x, latency stabilized. still seeing tokenization GIL stalls — might move tokenizer to worker pool or use rust binding.

perf-bot: perf summary: top symbols: PyObject_Call 22.3%, tokenize_fast 18.7%, memcpy 9.1%

jin: next steps: 1) instrument kernel selector to emit chosen kernel id + reason, 2) add async pinned allocation path in allocator, 3) experiment with merging tiny kernels into a single launch for prefetch stage to lower launch churn.

kai: i can prototype the kernel-selection telemetry and a small histogram of seq_len%64 vs chosen_kernel. will send a PR today. :thumbsup:

ashley: awesome. tagging @matt to review the batching suggestions. :eyes:

matt: on it. also can we add a perf tracepoint around KV cache lookup/evict to confirm miss->evict hot path? a few tracepoints in C++ would help correlate GIL stalls with device memcpy.
